provenance: Lane B, shard mutun-zad2, base 65bcdf60b800049bcf00bca9328e1bbd605fd88f: Zād al-Mustaqniʿ, kitāb al-ṭahāra from bāb al-ghusl to bāb al-ḥayḍ (b00008–b00011), one case per masʾala record, annotated for its leading ruling against the bank's readings and aligned with Ibn Rajab's furūʿ and ʿUmda's masāʾil, read in full from the locked witnesses. Candidate.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the ghusl is wājib (obligatory) by the emission (khurūj) of semen (al-manī) gushing and with pleasure, and not without them, except from one asleep («من غير نائم»). Follow-ons, the same need: semen that moves but does not come out obliges the ghusl («وإن انتقل ولم يخرج اغتسل له»), and its later exit is not a second cause («فإن خرج بعده لم يعده»). No reading of the bank enumerates what obliges the ghusl: cause_from_one_of_two (q014) decides whose ḥadath a found manī is, not what the cause (sabab) is.
cases.quote: وموجبه: خروج المني دفقا بلذة لا بدونهما
cases.expected: The ghusl is obligatory on the emission of manī gushing with pleasure (the sleeper excepted).

aligned.note: ʿUmda names the same cause, «خروج المني وهو الماء الدافق», beside the meeting of the circumcised parts; Zād adds pleasure («بلذة») and the sleeper's exception. They agree.

The sleeper who finds wetness he is not certain is manī: no ghusl by Aḥmad's naṣṣ, a riwāya obliges it. Zād's «من غير نائم» frees the sleeper from the gushing-and-pleasure condition, not from the certainty that it is manī.
Two who find manī in a garment they share: whose cause it is, not what the cause is.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the disappearance (taghyīb) of an original glans (ḥashafa) in an original farj, front or back, even of an animal or a dead body, obliges the ghusl. A domain rule on the causes (asbāb) of the ghusl; no reading decides it.
cases.quote: وتغييب حشفة "أصلية" في فرج "أصلي" قبلا كان أو دبرا ولو من بهيمة أو ميت
cases.expected: Penetration by the glans obliges the ghusl, even with an animal or a corpse.

aligned.note: ʿUmda's «والتقاء الختانين», the second cause it names. They agree; Zād adds the animal, the dead and the back passage.

cases.note: Leading ruling: a kāfir's Islām obliges the ghusl. Follow-ons, the same need: death, ḥayḍ (menstruation) and nifās (post-natal bleeding) oblige it; a birth without blood does not.
cases.quote: وإسلام كافر وموت وحيض ونفاس لا ولادة عارية عن دم
cases.expected: Islām of a kāfir, death, ḥayḍ and nifās oblige the ghusl; a bloodless birth does not.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: ḥayḍ «ويوجب الغسل». They agree on the ḥayḍ follow-on; ʿUmda's ghusl bāb does not name Islām or death.
ʿUmda: nifās takes ḥayḍ's rulings «فيما يحل ويحرم ويجب», the ghusl among them.

cases.note: Leading ruling: one on whom the ghusl is wājib (an obligation) may not recite the Qurʾān. Follow-ons: he may pass through the mosque for a need, and may not stay in it without wuḍūʾ. Ibn Rajab grounds the stay after wuḍūʾ in lightening the janāba (partial_capability, q008.f002: «ويستبيح به اللبث في المسجد عندنا»), but the leading prohibition of recitation is a domain rule no reading decides.
cases.quote: ومن لزمه الغسل حرم عليه قراءة القرآن
cases.expected: The junub may not recite the Qurʾān; he may cross the mosque for a need and stay in it only with wuḍūʾ.

aligned.note: The follow-on (staying in the mosque after wuḍūʾ) is stated there as a fruit of partial ghusl; its leading ruling is partial ghusl.
The parallel list for the ḥāʾiḍ (the menstruating woman): recitation and staying in the mosque are barred. Agrees in parallel.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the ghusl is sunna (recommended) for one who washed a corpse, or recovered from madness or fainting without a dream. A domain list of occasions; no reading decides it.
cases.quote: ومن غسل ميتا أو أفاق من جنون أو إغماء بلا حلم سن له الغسل
cases.expected: The ghusl is recommended after washing a corpse and on recovering from madness or fainting.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the complete ghusl: intention, then tasmiya, washing the hands thrice and what is soiled, wuḍūʾ, three handfuls on the head, then washing the whole body thrice. The sentence continues in b00008.p07 (rubbing, beginning on the right, washing the feet in another place), split at a page break; those acts are annotated here. A description of an act (ṣifa), a domain rule.
cases.quote: والغسل الكامل: أن ينوى ثم يسمي ويغسل يديه ثلاثا وما لوثه ويتوضأ ويحثي على رأسه ثلاثا1 ترويه ويعم بدنه غسلا ثلاثا
cases.expected: The complete ghusl is intention, tasmiya, the hands, wuḍūʾ, the head thrice, the body thrice, rubbing, the right first, the feet elsewhere.

aligned.note: ʿUmda gives the same sequence through Maymūna's ḥadīth (hands, private parts, wuḍūʾ, pouring, moving aside to wash the feet) and makes the rubbing (dalk) a practice. They agree.

cases.note: Not a masʾala: the second half of b00008.p06's sentence, split at the page break after «ويعم بدنه غسلا ثلاثا» (v01:p032 → p033) and listed in corpus/audit.json page_break_candidates. Its acts (rubbing, the right first, the feet elsewhere) are annotated with b00008.p06.

Leading ruling: the sufficient ghusl is intention, then tasmiya, and covering the body with water once. Zād counts the tasmiya in the sufficient (mujziʾ) ghusl, as it makes it wājib in wuḍūʾ; ʿUmda makes it sunna («وتسن التسمية»). The two mutun disagree; no reading decides the acts of the ghusl, so the disagreement is recorded here and does not enter the ledger.
cases.quote: والمجزئ: أن ينوي "ثم يسمي1" ويعم بدنه بالغسل مرة
cases.expected: The sufficient ghusl is intention, tasmiya and covering the body once.

positions.who: Zād: the tasmiya is part of the sufficient ghusl («والمجزئ: أن ينوي ثم يسمي»)

aligned.note: Same question. They disagree on the tasmiya (Zād in the mujziʾ, ʿUmda «وتسن التسمية»); ʿUmda names the rinsing of mouth and nose («مع المضمضة والاستنشاق») where Zād's «ويعم بدنه» is silent.

cases.note: Leading ruling: wuḍūʾ is done with a mudd and the ghusl with a ṣāʿ. Follow-ons: completing (isbāgh) with less suffices (the same need); intending both ḥadaths by one ghusl suffices («أو نوى بغسله الحدثين أجزأ»), which tadakhul gives (same kind, same purpose: discharged; q018.f000, «فالمذهب»). The leading measure is a domain rule.
cases.quote: ويتوضأ بمد ويغتسل بصاع
cases.expected: Wuḍūʾ with a mudd and ghusl with a ṣāʿ; less suffices if complete; one ghusl for both ḥadaths suffices.

aligned.note: The follow-on, one ghusl intending both ḥadaths, is the farʿ's question on its facts; Zād holds its madhhab side.
The same follow-on: «وإذا نوى بغسله الطهارتين أجزأ عنهما». They agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: for the junub, washing his private parts and wuḍūʾ before eating, sleeping or repeating intercourse are sunna. Ibn Rajab cites the same practice as given («كما يشرع للجنب إذا أراد النوم أو الوطء أو الأكل») to ground partial ghusl; the practice itself is a domain rule.
cases.quote: ويسن لجنب غسل فرجه والوضوء لأكل ونوم ولمعاودة وطء
cases.expected: Washing the private parts and wuḍūʾ are recommended for the junub before eating, sleep and repeated intercourse.

aligned.note: The farʿ (partial ghusl) cites this sunna as its premise, in the same words.

cases.note: A definition: tayammum is the substitute (badal) of purification by water. It states no facts, so substitute (q016, al-Saʿdī's rule of the badal) does not decide anything here; its condition (sharṭ) is stated in b00009.p02, which is derivable. What is missing is the classification that types tayammum as a badal of the water-ṭahāra (and whether it lifts the ḥadath, which Ibn Rajab denies «على المذهب»).
cases.quote: وهو: بدل طهارة الماء
cases.expected: Tayammum is the substitute of purification by water.

aligned.note: Ibn Rajab characterises tayammum between a general concession and a necessity-ṭahāra that does not lift the ḥadath («فإنه غير رافع له على المذهب»).

cases.quote: وعدم الماء أو زاد على ثمنه كثيرا أو بثمن1 يعجزه أو خاف باستعماله أو طلبه ضرر بدنه2 أو رفيقه أو حرمته أو ماله بعطش أو مرض أو هلاك ونحوه شرع التيمم
cases.note: SCOPED guard. Leading ruling: when the time of an obligatory (farḍ) prayer has entered (or a supererogatory one is permitted) and water is lacking, or costs much more than its price or a price he cannot pay, or its use or search harms his body, companion, household or property, tayammum is legislated. The inability is stated (original_possible false), so the substitute is used (substitute, al-Saʿdī's rule 28, q016). The time condition, a sharṭ (rule:tayammum_time_condition) and the price thresholds (rule:water_price_threshold) are not decided by the reading, so the guard is scoped and routing_label false.

aligned.note: ʿUmda's first condition, inability through absence, harm in use, thirst, fear in seeking it, or a high price; ʿUmda adds severe cold and the beast. They agree.
ʿUmda's second condition, the time («فلا يتيمم لفريضة قبل وقتها»). They agree.
The edge of the inability fact: water reached as the time runs out (al-Mughnī purifies after the time; al-Muḥarrar and the ẓāhir of Aḥmad: tayammum).

cases.quote: ومن وجد ماء يكفي بعض طهره تيمم بعد استعماله

positions.who: Zād and ʿUmda, stated decisively; the madhhab (al-Inṣāf: «وهو المذهب. وعليه الجمهور»): he uses it, then tayammum for the rest
the other wajh for the muḥdith (one in minor ḥadath): not obliged (Ibn Rajab q008.f003; Abū Bakr and Ibn Abī Mūsā per al-Inṣāf)

cases.note: Leading ruling: one who finds water enough for part of his purification (ṭahāra) uses it and then performs tayammum. Capable of part, the part not a pure means: he must do it (partial_capability, al-Saʿdī's rule 40, q008). Zād's «بعض طهره» covers both ḥadaths. For the junub there is no dispute (q008.f002, derivable); for the muḥdith Ibn Rajab reports two wujūh (q008.f003), so the case is an ikhtilāf, and Zād holds the reading's side, the madhhab in al-Inṣāf. Not decided by the reading: the order «بعد استعماله» and the wounded man's tayammum for the wound with washing (ghasl) the rest («ومن جرح تيمم له وغسل الباقي»).

aligned.note: The muḥdith's branch of Zād's general statement: the farʿ records the dispute.
The junub's branch: no dispute.
«فإن أمكنه استعماله في بعض بدنه أو وجد ماء لا يكفيه لطهارته استعمله وتيمم للباقي». They agree.
Its follow-on: partial water, tayammum for the rest, then water after the continuity (muwālāt) has lapsed: only the rest is washed.

cases.note: Leading ruling: he must seek water in his baggage, nearby and by asking for directions. A domain rule. Follow-on: one who forgot he could reach it and performed tayammum repeats («فإن نسي قدرته عليه وتيمم أعاد»). excused_error gives that on Ibn Rajab's own ground (q006.f005: the repetition for one who forgot the water in his baggage «مبني على أنه فرط بترك البحث والتحقيق»): no right of another, but negligent, so not excused.
cases.quote: ويجب طلب الماء في رحله وقربه وبدلالة
cases.expected: Seeking water is obligatory; one who forgot it and did tayammum repeats.

aligned.note: Its closing clause is this follow-on: the repetition for one who forgot the water in his baggage rests on negligence in searching.

cases.quote: وإن نوى بتيممه أحداثا
cases.note: SCOPED guard. Leading ruling: one who intends several ḥadaths by his tayammum prays and does not repeat; the sentence's apodosis «صلى ولم يعد» is printed in b00009.p06, split at a page break. One act, same kind and same purpose: it discharges them all (tadakhul, q018). Ibn Rajab: «ولو كان عادما للماء فتيمم تيمما واحدا ينوي به الحدثين أجزأه عنهما بغير خلاف ونص عليه أحمد في رواية مهنا», so derivable, not an ikhtilāf. The sentence's other branches are not decided by the reading: tayammum for bodily najāsa harmful to remove or with nothing to remove it (rule:tayammum_for_bodily_najasa), fear of cold or confinement in a town (rule:no_repeat_after_excused_tayammum), lacking both water and earth (rule:faqid_al_tahurayn).

aligned.note: The farʿ's tayammum follow-on is this question on its facts, «بغير خلاف».
«وكذلك لو تيمم للحدثين والنجاسة على بدنه أجزأ عن جميعها». They agree.
One with only a najis garment or place prays in it and does not repeat: parallel to Zād's no-repeat branches.

cases.note: Not a masʾala: the second half of b00009.p05's sentence, split at the page break after «أو عدم» (v01:p033 → p034) and listed in corpus/audit.json page_break_candidates. Its apodosis «صلى ولم يعد» and its branches (cold, confinement, lacking both water and earth) are annotated with b00009.p05.
Leading ruling: tayammum is with purifying (ṭahūr) earth that has dust, not altered by another pure substance. A domain rule of the means; no reading decides it.
cases.quote: ويجب التيمم بتراب طهور له غبار لم يغيره طاهر غيره1
cases.expected: Tayammum requires ṭahūr earth with dust.

aligned.note: «فلا يتيمم إلا بتراب طاهر له غبار». They agree: al-Inṣāf reads «طاهر» in this wording as the purifying earth («مراده بقوله " بتراب طاهر " التراب الطهور»).

cases.note: Leading ruling: the obligatory acts (farḍ, «فروضه») of tayammum are wiping the face and the hands to the wrists, with order (tartīb) and continuity (muwālāt) in the minor ḥadath. A domain rule.
cases.quote: وفروضه: مسح وجهه ويديه إلى كوعيه والترتيب والموالاة
cases.expected: Tayammum's obligatory acts: face, hands to the wrists, order and continuity in minor ḥadath.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: the face and the palms («وجهه وكفيه»). They agree on the extent; ʿUmda does not list order and continuity.

cases.note: Leading ruling: tayammum requires the intention of what it is for, a ḥadath or other (a najāsa). Follow-ons: intending one does not suffice for the other; intending a supererogatory (nafl) prayer, or no specification, does not permit an obligatory one; intending an obligatory one permits obligatory and supererogatory prayers for its whole time. tadakhul would decide «فإن نوى أحدها لم يجزئه عن الآخر» given a fact for intending each act: Ibn Rajab's qāʿida makes the discharge a sharṭ-bound one on intending both («يشترط أن ينويهما جميعا على المشهور»), but the reading has no such fact.
cases.quote: وتشترط النية لما تيمم له من حدث أو غيره
cases.expected: Tayammum requires specifying its intention; one intention does not cover another; a nafl intention does not permit a farḍ.

aligned.note: ʿUmda's third condition: for a nafl he may not pray a farḍ; for a farḍ he prays it and what he wishes until its time ends. They agree.
«وإن نوى بعضها فليس له إلا ما نوى». They agree.
The discharge by one act when both are intended («إذا نوى الطهارتين [جميعا] بها»).

cases.note: Leading ruling: tayammum is voided (bāṭil, «ويبطل») by the end of the time, by what voids wuḍūʾ, and by finding water, even during the prayer, not after it. The list is a domain rule. Its last item is Ibn Rajab's q007.f001 (switch_to_original: necessity, so the prayer is void; two riwāyas there), and Zād states that side, the madhhab in al-Inṣāf («هذا المذهب بلا ريب»); «لا بعدها» (no repetition once it is over) is the same need.
cases.quote: ويبطل التيمم بخروج الوقت
cases.expected: Tayammum is voided by the end of the time, the nullifiers of wuḍūʾ, and finding water even in the prayer, not after it.

aligned.note: The water-during-prayer item, on the farʿ's facts.
Water found after tayammum and before the prayer bars entering it.
Two prayers joined by tayammum in the time of the first, then water in the second's time: it suffices (the end of the time against what was done in it).
«ويبطل التيمم ما يبطل طهارة الماء وخروج الوقت والقدرة على استعمال الماء وإن كان في الصلاة». They agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: for one who hopes to find water, tayammum at the end of the time is better. A domain rule of preference; substitute decides only that the badal is used when the original is impossible.
cases.quote: والتيمم آخر الوقت لراجي الماء أولى
cases.expected: Delaying tayammum to the end of the time is better for one who hopes for water.

aligned.note: The same tension between the time and the water: one who reaches water as the time runs out.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the manner of tayammum: intention, tasmiya, striking the earth with the fingers spread, wiping the face with their insides and the palms with the hands, and passing between the fingers. A description (ṣifa).
cases.quote: وصفته: أن ينوى ثم يسمي ويضرب التراب بيديه مفرجتي الأصابع يمسح وجهه بباطنهما وكفيه براحتيه ويخلل أصابعه
cases.expected: Tayammum: intention, tasmiya, one strike, face then palms.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: one strike, face and palms; ʿUmda allows more strikes or more wiping («وإن تيمم بأكثر من ضربة أو مسح أكثر جاز»). They agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: for every najāsa on the ground, one washing (ghasl) that removes its substance suffices. Follow-ons, the same need: elsewhere seven, one of them with earth, for the dog and the pig (ushnān and the like may replace the earth); for other najāsāt seven without earth (continued in b00010.p02, split at a page break).
cases.quote: يجزئ في غسل النجاسات كلها إذا كانت على الأرض غسلة واحدة تذهب بعين النجاسة
cases.expected: On the ground one washing that removes the substance suffices; elsewhere seven (one with earth for dog and pig).

aligned.note: They agree on the ground («فصبة واحد تذهب بعينها») and on seven with earth for dog and pig; they disagree on other najāsāt: ʿUmda «ويجزئ في سائر النجاسات ثلاث منقية», Zād seven without earth.
A najis vessel dipped in running water with seven flows: one washing or seven.

cases.note: Not a masʾala: the end of b00010.p01's sentence («وفي» / «نجاسة غيرهما سبع بلا تراب»), split at the page break (v01:p034 → p035) and listed in corpus/audit.json page_break_candidates. Annotated with b00010.p01.

Leading ruling: a thing made najis is not purified by sun, wind, rubbing or transformation (istiḥāla), except wine (that turns to vinegar by itself). istihlak (q022) concerns a substance submerged in another so that its trace does not show, not the transformation of the najis thing itself, so it is not forced. Follow-ons: wine made vinegar by an act is not purified, nor a liquid oil made najis (the same need); a hidden spot of najāsa is washed (ghasl) until its removal is certain (certainty over belief, as asl_zahir has at q159.f007).
cases.quote: ولا يطهر متنجس بشمس ولا ريح ولا دلك ولا استحالة غير الخمرة
cases.expected: Sun, wind, rubbing and transformation do not purify, except wine turning to vinegar.

aligned.note: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb's way: water transforms the najāsa («بل الماء أحالها»), the cognate question whether transformation removes the ruling.
Tanning the dead animal's skin does not purify it «على ظاهر المذهب».
Wine that turns to vinegar in the usurper's hand must be returned: the exception «غير الخمرة».
The hidden-spot follow-on: certain najāsa is not removed by preponderant belief.
The hidden-spot follow-on: «وإن خفي موضع النجاسة من الثوب أو غيره غسل ما تيقن به غسلها». They agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the urine of a boy who has not eaten food is purified by sprinkling (naḍḥ), becoming ṭāhir. A domain rule.
cases.quote: ويطهر بول غلام لم يأكل الطعام بنضحه
cases.expected: A nursing boy's urine is purified by sprinkling.

aligned.note: «ويجزئ في بول الغلام الذي لم يأكل الطعام النضح». They agree; ʿUmda adds madhy.

cases.note: Leading ruling: outside liquids and food, a small amount of najis blood from a pure (ṭāhir) animal is excused. Follow-on: the trace left by istijmār (wiping with stones) is excused (the same need). tolerance_exceeded (q029) decides what an excess over a tolerated amount forfeits, not which amounts are tolerated.
cases.quote: ويعفى "في غير مائع ومطعوم" عن يسير دم نجس "من حيوان طاهر"
cases.expected: A small amount of blood, outside liquids and food, and the trace of istijmār are excused.

aligned.note: «ويعفي عن يسيره ويسير الدم وما تولد منه من القيح والصديد». They agree.
Ibn ʿAqīl's analogy: a large najāsa in a garment is washed whole, its tolerated part not singled out.

cases.note: Leading ruling: a human does not become najis by death, nor an animal without flowing blood born of something pure (ṭāhir). hair_detached (q002) decides whether hair and nails follow the body, not whether death makes the body najis.
cases.quote: ولا ينجس الآدمي بالموت ولا ما3 لا نفس له سائلة "متولد من طاهر"
cases.expected: A dead human and a bloodless creature born of pure matter are not najis.

aligned.note: «وكل ميتة نجسة إلا الآدمي ... وما لا نفس له سائلة إذا لم يكن متولدا من النجاسات». They agree.
Hair does not become najis by death, and a part separated from a human not «على الصحيح».

cases.note: Leading ruling: the urine, semen (al-manī) and dung of an animal whose meat is eaten are pure (ṭāhir, not najis). Follow-ons, the same need: human semen (manī), the moisture of a woman's farj, the leftover (suʾr) of a cat and of what is smaller are pure.
cases.quote: وبول ما يؤكل لحمه ومنيه وروثه طاهر
cases.expected: The urine, semen and dung of edible animals, human semen, a woman's moisture and a cat's leftover are pure.

aligned.note: «ومني الآدمي وبول ما يؤكل لحمه طاهر». They agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: predatory beasts and birds, the domestic donkey and the mule bred from it are najis. A domain catalogue; no reading decides it. ʿUmda's ṭahāra has no counterpart.
cases.quote: وسباع البهائم والطير والحمار الأهلي والبغل منه نجسه
cases.expected: Predatory beasts and birds, the domestic donkey and the mule are najis.

cases.note: Leading ruling: there is no ḥayḍ (menstruation) before nine full years, nor after fifty, nor with pregnancy. ʿUmda puts the upper age at sixty («وأكثره ستون»), so the mutun disagree; no reading decides the bounds, so the disagreement is recorded here and not in the ledger.
cases.quote: لا حيض قبل تمام تسع سنين ولا بعد خمسين سنة ولا مع حمل
cases.expected: No ḥayḍ before nine years, after fifty, or in pregnancy.

positions.who: ʿUmda b00009.p02: «وأقل سن تحيض له المرأة تسع سنين وأكثره ستون»

aligned.note: They agree on nine; they disagree on the upper limit: ʿUmda sixty, Zād fifty.
«والحامل لا تحيض»: they agree; ʿUmda adds that blood a day or two before birth is nifās.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the least ḥayḍ is a day and a night, the most fifteen, the usual six or seven; the least purity (ṭahāra), the ṭuhr, between two ḥayḍs is thirteen days, and the most has no limit. Domain bounds.
cases.quote: وأقله يوم وليلة وأكثره خمسة عشر1 وغالبه ست أو سبع
cases.expected: Ḥayḍ: least a day and night, most fifteen, usual six or seven; least ṭuhr thirteen, no upper limit.

aligned.note: The same four bounds. They agree.
The usual six or seven («لأنه غالب عادة النساء»). They agree.
«وأكثر الحيض على ظاهر المذهب خمسة عشر يوما», as a premise of woman's half.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the ḥāʾiḍ (menstruating woman) makes up the fast, not the prayer. A domain rule. Follow-ons: neither is valid from her and both are forbidden; intercourse in the farj is forbidden, with a kaffāra of a dīnār or half (rule:hayd_intercourse_kaffara); enjoyment below the farj is permitted, which supervening_bar_extends_to_preliminaries gives (q136.f000: not a worship, weak_ownership false, so the preliminaries stay permitted; the madhhab side); after the blood stops and before the ghusl only fasting and ṭalāq are permitted.
cases.quote: وتقضي الحائض الصوم لا الصلاة
cases.expected: The ḥāʾiḍ makes up fasting, not prayer; intercourse is forbidden with a kaffāra; enjoyment below the farj is permitted.

aligned.note: «الحائض والنفساء تفطران وتقضيان». They agree.
Prayer is not obligatory on the ḥāʾiḍ. They agree.
Ḥayḍ bars prayer and its obligation, fasting and intercourse in the farj. They agree.
After the blood stops fasting and ṭalāq are permitted, and enjoyment below the farj («اصنعوا كل شيء غير النكاح»). They agree; ʿUmda states no kaffāra.
The enjoyment follow-on, on the farʿ's facts; Zād holds its madhhab side.
The kaffāra when ḥayḍ begins during intercourse.
The ḥāʾiḍ purified during a day of Ramaḍān makes it up.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the beginner (al-mubtadaʾa) sits out the least ḥayḍ, then washes (ghusl) and prays; if it stops at the most or less she washes when it stops, and once repeated three times it is ḥayḍ and she makes up what fell due in it. Follow-ons: beyond the most she is mustaḥāḍa; she follows discernment (black over red) and otherwise the usual ḥayḍ. As worded, ʿUmda treats blood within the most as ḥayḍ from the first month («وإن جاوز ذلك ولم يعبر أكثر الحيض فهو حيض»), the habit forming by three months; Zād sits only the least until it repeats. Ibn Rajab's contrast at q106.f001 gives the make-up: the beginner's doubtful days become known by repetition, so they are not treated as non-existent (unknown_as_nonexistent: unknown, no despair, so false).
cases.quote: والمبتدأة تجلس أقله ثم تغتسل وتصلي
cases.expected: The beginner sits the least ḥayḍ, then washes and prays; after three repetitions it is ḥayḍ and she makes up what fell due.

positions.ruling: sits the least, then washes and prays until three repetitions
blood within the most is ḥayḍ from the first month

aligned.note: They disagree as worded: ʿUmda sits all blood within the most as ḥayḍ, Zād the least until three repetitions.
Discernment: «فحيضها زمن الأسود الثخين». They agree.
No discernment: six or seven days. They agree.
«بخلاف الزائد على الأقل في حق المبتدأة على ظاهر المذهب حيث تقضي الصوم الواقع فيه قبل ثبوت العادة بالتكرار»: Zād's make-up follow-on.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the mustaḥāḍa (one with continuous bleeding) who has a habit sits her habit, even if she has discernment; if she forgot it she follows a fit («الصالح») discernment, else the usual ḥayḍ; the cases of one who knows the number but forgot the place, and of a habit that grows or moves, follow. asl_zahir derives only the third tier (q159.f014: the usual six or seven, the ẓāhir of resemblance over the aṣl); habit over discernment is a domain rule.
cases.quote: والمستحاضة المعتادة ولو مميزة تجلس عادتها
cases.expected: The mustaḥāḍa with a habit sits her habit even with discernment; else discernment; else the usual ḥayḍ.

aligned.note: The same tiers, habit, then discernment, then the usual ḥayḍ; the farʿ's case annotates the third.
«فإن كانت معتادة فحيضها أيام عادتها» and otherwise discernment. They agree.
The one who forgot her habit and has no discernment: six or seven. They agree.
The days beyond what the mustaḥāḍa sits are treated as non-existent.

cases.note: Leading ruling: yellowness (ṣufra) and turbidity (kudra) in the time of the habit are ḥayḍ. Follow-on, continued in b00011.p07 after a page break: a day of blood and a day of purity: the blood is ḥayḍ and the clean day ṭuhr (ṭahāra), unless it passes the most (talfīq). Domain rules.
cases.quote: والصفرة والكدرة في زمن العادة حيض
cases.expected: Yellowness and turbidity in the habit's time are ḥayḍ; alternate days of blood and purity are each ruled as such.

cases.note: Not a masʾala: the second half of b00011.p06's sentence («ومن رأت يوما دما» / «ويوما نقاء فالدم حيض…»), split at the page break (v01:p036 → p037) and listed in corpus/audit.json page_break_candidates. Annotated with b00011.p06.

Leading ruling: the mustaḥāḍa and those like her wash the farj, bandage it and perform wuḍūʾ for the time of each prayer, then pray farḍ and nafl prayers. Follow-ons: she is not approached except on fear of ʿanat (hardship of abstinence), as Ibn ʿAqīl has at q112.f002; a ghusl for each prayer is recommended.
cases.quote: والمستحاضة ونحوها تغسل فرجها وتعصبه وتتوضأ لوقت كل صلاة
cases.expected: The mustaḥāḍa washes, binds and performs wuḍūʾ for each prayer's time; intercourse only on fear of ʿanat.

aligned.note: «وتغسل فرجها وتعصبه وتتوضأ لوقت كل صلاة وتصلي وكذا حكم من به سلس البول». They agree.
Ibn ʿAqīl: intercourse with the mustaḥāḍa is permitted only on fear of ʿanat.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the most nifās (post-natal bleeding) is forty days. Follow-ons: if her ṭahāra comes before it she purifies and prays, and intercourse before the forty is disliked; blood returning within them is doubtful: she fasts, prays and makes up the wājib fast. Ibn Rajab gives that make-up («وكذلك النفاس المشكوك فيه تقضي فيه الصوم ; لأنه لا يتكرر», q106.f001).
cases.quote: وأكثر مدة النفاس أربعون يوما
cases.expected: Nifās lasts at most forty days; blood returning within them is doubtful.

aligned.note: They agree on forty and on purity before it; they disagree on blood returning within the forty: ʿUmda «فهو نفاس أيضا», Zād doubtful.
The doubtful-nifās follow-on.

cases.note: Leading ruling: nifās is like ḥayḍ in what it permits, forbids, obliges and lifts, except the ʿidda and puberty. Follow-on: with twins, nifās begins and ends from the first (rule:nifas_durations). A domain assimilation; tabaa (q133) decides what follows its base in proof, not this.
cases.quote: وهو كالحيض فيما يحل ويحرم ويجب ويسقط غير العدة
cases.expected: Nifās is like ḥayḍ except for ʿidda and puberty; with twins it counts from the first.

aligned.note: «وحكمها حكم الحيض فيما يحل ويحرم ويجب ويسقط به». They agree; Zād adds the exceptions.
